subject: german
title: Stamp 2: Public Broadcasting
welcome_lead: Stamp Germany's distinctive public broadcasting system.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on ARD, ZDF, public broadcasting, and the Rundfunkbeitrag.

concepts.def: Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Rundfunkanstalten Deutschlands; consortium of regional public broadcasters.
Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen; national public TV channel based in Mainz.
Broadcasting fee paid by every household (around 18 euros per month).
ARD's flagship 8 p.m. news, watched by millions daily.
National public radio offering news and culture; part of Deutschlandradio.
Private broadcasters such as RTL and ProSiebenSat.1, dependent on advertising.

walkthroughs.body_html: Germany has a duales System: public broadcasters financed by the Rundfunkbeitrag plus private broadcasters financed by advertising. The Constitutional Court has repeatedly defended public service media.
The 15-minute Tagesschau on ARD at 20:00 is Germany's most-watched news. Its sober, neutral tone has been a fixture of public discourse for decades.

Every household pays the Rundfunkbeitrag (currently about 18.36 EUR per month), regardless of usage. This guarantees independence from advertisers, though critics question both its level and necessity.
